ai.title: CLI slash menu tracks pasted content
ai.summary: CLI slash menu detection now checks `this.pastedContent` alongside `this.rl.line` in `npm-app/src/cli.ts`. This prevents the menu from activating when a slash is pasted as part of a larger string, ensuring it only appears when `/` is the first character typed. Scope limited to internal CLI logic.

eli5.text: When you're typing in the command-line assistant and you press the slash key to bring up the quick menu of commands, the menu will now correctly appear only if the slash is the very first character you've entered. If you paste in a longer string that happens to contain a slash (like a file path or sentence), the assistant won't mistakenly show the menu. Previously, it would check only what was on the current line; now it also considers any content that was pasted in. This makes the slash menu behave more predictably, so you don't get unexpected menu popups interrupting your pasted text. The change is live today and affects anyone using the command-line version of the assistant.

The app quietly updated to a new numbered release, which is why you might see a fresh version number the next time you open it or install it. Behind the scenes, this release also switched the large file search and replace feature to use a newer AI model, lets the CLI slash menu properly track content you paste in, and adds a new grading system that uses an AI judge to evaluate how well the file picker works. If you use the CLI or work with large files, you'll get the benefits of these changes automatically just by updating. Nothing about your access or available features changes today; this just keeps the software current for future improvements.

ai.title: Startup menu homedir check
ai.summary: Updated startup menu logic in npm-app/src/menu.ts to detect homedir via path.relative instead of strict equality. Improved onboarding text and ensured clean exit with process.exit(0). Internal change.

eli5.text: When you open Codebuff while sitting in your home folder (or the root of your hard drive), it now correctly recognizes that you aren't inside a real project and shows you a brief welcome message with setup steps, then quietly closes itself. Previously, the check that guessed 'you’re not in a project' was too strict, so some people would get the message even when they were working inside an actual project. That comparison now works more flexibly, the welcome text was rewritten slightly, and the program exits cleanly instead of leaving anything behind.

ai.title: Tweak startup wording in npm-app menu
ai.summary: Updated `displayGreeting` in `npm-app/src/menu.ts` to clarify Codebuff's role as an AI pair programmer and fix a typo in the navigation instructions. The message now explicitly states the current project root and advises running `codebuff` within the target directory. This change is internal to the CLI startup experience.

eli5.text: When you start the assistant, the welcome message now tells you that it is your AI pair programmer that edits your codebase through natural conversation, shows the folder you are currently in, and says to run the command from within your project directory. If you saw this screen today, you would notice the friendlier wording, the fixed spelling of "Navigate", and the example path printed in color instead of plain text. This only affects the startup screen shown when the project folder is inside your home directory.

ai.title: Enable relace for larger files
ai.summary: LARGE_FILE_TOKEN_LIMIT increased from 16_000 to 64_000 in backend/src/process-file-block.ts. Temporary relace dispatch logic for files under 64k tokens removed. Routing to handleLargeFile now triggers at higher threshold.

eli5.text: You can now use the assistant's smart replace feature on larger files without it timing out or giving up partway through. Files used to be split into smaller pieces when they got too big, but now the system can handle bigger chunks at once, roughly four times larger than before, so you wait less and the replace works on more of your file in a single pass. This change is live today.

ai.title: Switch large file search/replace model to o4-mini
ai.summary: Update model for large file search/replace operations in `backend/src/process-file-block.ts` from `models.o3mini` to `models.o4mini`. This internal change leverages the newer model for improved performance in this specific backend process. No user-facing features or configurations are affected.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to search through or replace text inside a very large file, that behind-the-scenes step now uses a newer version of the helper the assistant talks to. Nothing about how or where you type, or which settings you pick, changes. The effect you might notice: those big-file edits come back a little faster or get answered a bit more reliably, but only if you happen to open a file large enough to trigger that specific path.

ai.title: Update Gemini 2.5 Flash preview model to 05-20
ai.summary: The `gemini2_5_flash` and `gemini2_5_flash_thinking` constants in `common/src/constants.ts` updated from `gemini-2.5-flash-preview-04-17` to `gemini-2.5-flash-preview-05-20`. This aligns Freebuff with the latest upstream preview release. The change affects the core model definitions used across CLI, Web, and Desktop surfaces.

eli5.text: The AI model that powers the assistant behind the scenes has been swapped for a newer preview version dated May 20. Anyone using the assistant across the app, website, or desktop will now be running responses through this updated model, which may produce slightly different wording or reasoning. If you looked at the code, you'd see the model's name reference changed from the April 17 version to the May 20 one. There's nothing you have to do; you'll just start getting answers from the newer preview automatically.

ai.title: Add start-lite dev script
ai.summary: Added `start-lite` npm scripts to root and `npm-app` package.json. Mirrors existing `start-max` pattern but passes `--lite` flag to CLI entrypoint. Internal dev tooling only; no user-facing behavior change.

eli5.text: The development team added a new shortcut for running the app in a lighter, faster mode during internal testing. It works just like the existing full version shortcut, but tells the app to skip heavy features for quicker startup. This only affects developers working on the code today and won't change anything for regular users.

ai.title: xml-stream-parser ignores new params while parsing existing
ai.summary: xml-stream-parser.ts now ignores new parameters encountered while parsing an existing parameter, emitting the raw tag as text instead of ending the current parameter. This prevents premature parameter closure and data loss when malformed XML contains nested or unexpected tags. The change affects backend stream processing logic and updates the warning message to instruct users to escape XML. Tests in xml-stream-parser.test.ts reflect the new behavior where state remains unchanged and rawTag is passed to onText.

eli5.text: When the system reads incoming message text that contains unexpected formatting tags inside an already open field, it no longer breaks the field or drops the content. Instead, it keeps the current field open and treats the unexpected tag as plain text, showing a warning that reminds you to close all fields and escape XML characters. This affects anyone sending structured data that has stray tags, like malformed API responses or badly formatted integrations, and it prevents silent data loss where fields would unexpectedly close early.

ai.title: Add attribute to xml-stream-parser test case
ai.summary: Updated the 'ignore new parameters' test case in `backend/src/__tests__/xml-stream-parser.test.ts` to include an attribute (`attr="123"`) within the nested `<param2>` tag. This ensures the stream parser correctly ignores parameters with attributes while preserving raw text content in the final result.

eli5.text: The program's self-check was updated to handle one specific case it previously missed: an XML tag that includes an attribute (like a tag with extra data attached to it). This only affects the internal testing process used by the developers, not anything you'd directly experience. When the self-check runs, it now confirms the program correctly ignores extra tags with attributes while still keeping the main content intact. This change is live today as part of the development workflow, ensuring future updates don't accidentally break that behavior.

ai.title: Fix XML entity parsing in saxy
ai.summary: Updated parseEntities in common/src/util/saxy.ts to correctly handle malformed or invalid XML entities. The logic now treats ampersands followed by invalid characters (space, &, <, >) or empty strings as literal characters, preventing incorrect parsing. Numeric entities (decimal and hex) are parsed with explicit validation, falling back to literal passthrough on NaN. This fix applies to the shared core utility used by all Freebuff surfaces.

eli5.text: When you type something containing the ampersand symbol followed by certain characters, the app can sometimes misread it and display text incorrectly, especially if the ampersand isn’t meant to be a special code symbol. The app now handles those awkward ampersand cases more carefully, so it shows what you actually typed instead of getting confused. This affects any feature across the app that takes in text containing ampersands, like forms, commands, or pasted content. If you previously saw strange characters or missing text when typing ampersands, you’ll now see your input appear as expected.

ai.title: Add XML entity escaping instructions to tool definitions
ai.summary: Updated `backend/src/tools.ts` to explicitly instruct agents on escaping XML entities. Added rule requiring `&lt;` for literal `<` strings to prevent accidental tool execution or parsing errors. Internal prompt refinement only.

eli5.text: The instructions tell the assistant how to write angle brackets and other special characters when showing or saving text, so a less-than sign meant as literal text no longer risks being mistaken for the start of a command. If you looked at the relevant internal guide, you would see a short new section spelling out the safer way to write those characters. It is live now, and it only affects how the assistant formats its own output.
